findings.evidence: template/scripts/independent_review.py risky_paths: `base_ref = f"origin/{read_platform_config(root)['main_branch']}"`; review_state: `except RuntimeError as exc:  # finish stops on this; a status view reports it.`
findings.summary: review_state only catches RuntimeError around review_is_required, but risky_paths reads read_platform_config(root)['main_branch'] directly. A missing key raises KeyError and crashes the status view, where the other failure causes are reported as an 'unknown' state.

findings.evidence: specs/completion-lifecycle/spec.md line 256: 'a missing or stale review of a managed change SHALL be run outside archive before finalize'; the 'Quick task' scenario there covers only the no-protected-path case.
findings.summary: The modified requirement 'Required independent review is an automatic, resumable lifecycle gate' still speaks only of 'a missing or stale review of a managed change'. Its scenarios (archive, finalize, resume) are managed-only. The new quick-task behavior sits in separate added requirements, so the contract text reads as managed-only and contradicts the 'quick and managed alike' rule.
